units.function: A monolithic developer-operator subsystem for creating, initializing, cloning, repairing, reseeding, listing, merging and deleting Git worktree-local Paperclip instances. It manages configuration, environment, Secrets keys, embedded PostgreSQL, backups/restores/migrations, execution quarantine, storage objects, Git hooks/dependencies and cross-database history import.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI command -> worktree helper libraries plus config/env/home/path utilities -> direct @paperclipai/db schema, migration, backup and storage operations -> Git, filesystem, process environment, sockets, embedded PostgreSQL, S3 and package-manager execution. The command bypasses stable service/API/port boundaries and owns deployment, data-plane, credential and domain migration behavior.
units.keyDataModels: Worktree config/env/instance paths and branding; seed pending/complete/lock markers; source/target PaperclipConfig; shared Agent JWT Secret and Secrets master key; database snapshots and migrations; Agent heartbeat/runtime state; issues/comments/documents/revisions/assets/projects/workspaces/goals; storage object keys; merge plans and identity-clearing adjustments.
units.lifecycle: Create/repair Git worktree -> optionally fetch and execute dependency installation -> write target config/env and clone identity/Secrets authority -> snapshot/reset/restore/migrate database -> quarantine copied execution and pause schedules unless overridden -> optionally merge selected histories/assets through a preview plus SQL transaction -> expose all env entries -> cleanup Git branch/worktree and recursively delete instance data. Local locks/markers cover lazy seeding but not the full cross-resource lifecycle.
units.testAssessment: Reuse of completed evidence: the worktree test unit exercised 43 cases, with 37 passed, 2 macOS path-canonicalization failures and 4 embedded-PostgreSQL skips; sandboxed port probing additionally exposed an unbounded exhaustion path. The merge-history helper suite passed 8/8 and specifies deterministic planning/adjustment cases. Coverage is substantial for helpers and safety branches but does not prove cross-resource rollback, real launchd/systemd/PostgreSQL/S3 behavior, large histories, concurrent source/target mutations, asset-byte integrity, authorization, responsibility preservation or destructive-change evidence.
units.designRationale: A disposable branch-scoped instance lets developers experiment with production-shaped data while reducing accidental duplicate Agent execution. Stable IDs, execution quarantine, paused schedules, workspace rebinding, explicit preview and idempotent insert checks address real clone-and-merge failure modes. Lazy seed markers reduce startup cost and the exclusive token lock prevents duplicate local clones.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs safe local-enterprise/FDE sandboxes, tenant-scoped sanitized Demo or staging clones, portable evidence/history, execution fencing and reversible deployment/data migration without duplicating legal identity, credentials, authorization contracts or live Agent ownership.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT behind separate Deployment, EnvironmentSnapshot, DataExport/Import, SecretRebinding and ExecutionFence ports. Adapt the seed generation marker, token-safe local lock, default execution quarantine, paused schedule, stable-ID merge preview and identity-clearing concepts. Require a signed source snapshot manifest, data-classification policy, accountable human approval bound to a plan digest, per-Connector credential rebinding, staged content-addressed blobs, transactional finalize/rollback and immutable migration evidence. Git worktrees remain a developer adapter, never the canonical product environment model.
units.responsibilityConflict: The command can clone decryptable Secrets, shared Agent signing authority, human-authored records and live assignments, overwrite databases, import identity-bearing history and delete instance data based only on local CLI access and optional prompts. It cannot prove data-export authorization, accountable human intent, source snapshot identity, permission/Connector rebinding or who owns copied work; escape hatches intentionally preserve runnable source assignments or mutate a live target.

units.securityFindings: CRITICAL: worktree env prints all adjacent env entries as JSON or shell exports, including database URLs and signing/credential values. CRITICAL: seeding copies the local-encrypted master key and shared Agent JWT Secret alongside a database clone, reproducing decryptable Secrets and identity authority without a governed export/rebinding ceremony. HIGH: preserve-live-work can retain runnable assignments/timers and allow-live-target can overwrite a database while detected running; repair invokes destructive reseed/force paths with internal yes=true. HIGH: force cleanup can recursively delete a worktree, unique commits, uncommitted changes and instance data without an approved manifest or recovery journal. HIGH: attachment bodies are written to external storage inside a SQL transaction without size/SHA-256 verification or rollback, permitting orphaned/overwritten objects and DB/blob divergence. HIGH: preview/confirmation is not bound to source/target revisions or a content digest, and --yes bypasses it. MEDIUM: package installation executes fetched repository lifecycle scripts; Git hooks, including symlinks, are recursively copied into worktree Git state. MEDIUM: whole-company histories and blobs are buffered without pagination/limits; port allocation and several filesystem checks are check-then-act; fixed embedded PostgreSQL credentials rely solely on loopback/isolation; PID locks can wait indefinitely and stale cleanup is manual. Positive controls include tenant-prefixed normalized object keys, migration-state checks, seed locking, quarantining Agent execution, pausing schedules, stable-ID imports, atomic issue-counter reservation and explicit unsupported-run disclosure.
